'''Igor Ivanovich Belanov''' ({{langx|ru|И́горь Ива́нович Бела́нов}}) or '''Ihor Ivanovych Bielanov''' ({{langx|uk|Ігор Іванович Бєланов}}; born 25 September 1960) is a Soviet and Ukrainian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[striker (association football)|striker]].

He made a name for himself at [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]], winning five major titles as well as the [[Ballon d'Or]] in [[1986 Ballon d'Or|1986]] and became the second [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] national to win the award after [[Oleg Blokhin|Oleh Blokhin]] ([[1975 Ballon d'Or|1975]]). He then spent six years in Germany with [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] in the [[Bundesliga]] and [[Eintracht Braunschweig]] in the [[2. Bundesliga]], with little success.

Belanov represented the [[Soviet Union national football team|Soviet Union]] at [[1986 FIFA World Cup|one]] [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 1988|one]] [[UEFA European Football Championship|European Championship]]. He was included in the list of the top 100 World Cup footballers of all time by ''[[The Guardian]]'' in 2014.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2014/may/27/the-world-cups-top-100-footballers-of-all-time-interactive The World Cup's top 100 footballers of all time – interactive]. ''The Guardian''. 27 May 2014</ref> In 2011, he, [[Oleg Blokhin|Oleh Blokhin]] and [[Vitaliy Starukhin]] were named as the "legends of Ukrainian football" at the Victory of Football awards.<ref>{{cite news|access-date=11 September 2013 |url=http://www.bulvar.com.ua/arch/2011/51/4ef313ba6efb7/ |script-title=ru:Лучшими футболистами Украины признаны Анатолий Тимощук, Андрей Шевченко и Александр Шовковский |language=ru |publisher=bulvar.com.ua |date=20 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015040522/http://www.bulvar.com.ua/arch/2011/51/4ef313ba6efb7/ |url-status=live |archive-date=15 October 2013}}</ref>

==Club career==

===Beginnings and Dynamo Kyiv===
Belanov was born in [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], [[Soviet Union]]. He started playing professionally in his hometown, with [[SC Odesa|SKA Odesa]] and [[FC Chornomorets Odesa]], joining country giants [[FC Dynamo Kyiv]] in 1985, and scoring ten goals in [[1985 Soviet Top League|his first season]], which ended with [[Soviet Top League|league]] and [[Soviet Cup|cup]] conquest.

Along with teammates [[Oleg Blokhin|Oleh Blokhin]] and [[Oleksandr Zavarov]], Belanov led the scoring charts at the [[1985–86 European Cup Winners' Cup|1985–86]] [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] (five apiece) as Dynamo won the competition for the second time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec2tops.html |title=Cup Winners Cup Top Scorers |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|access-date=15 September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922042146/http://www.rsssf.com/ec/ec2tops.html |url-status=live |archive-date=22 September 2008}}</ref> He played the full 90 minutes in [[1986 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|the final]] against [[Atlético Madrid]] (3–0).

===Germany===
Midway through 1989, 29-year-old Belanov got the long-awaited clearance to join a [[Western Europe]]an side, making a move to Germany to join [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]]. He joined for a transfer fee of 2 million [[Deutsche Mark]] but did not move until October due to wanting to conclude the Soviet season; he was then sidelined by muscle fibre injury.<ref name=welt/> His debut in the [[Bundesliga]] came on 4 November 1989 in a 4–0 away defeat against [[VfB Stuttgart]], but he failed to impress overall, scoring only five goals in his one-and-a-half-season stint.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/players/ibelanovdata.html | title = Ihor Ivanovych Belanov – Matches and Goals in Bundesliga | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 24 June 2020 | access-date = 29 June 2020 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF.com]]}}</ref>

Belanov's reputation at the club diminished further in January 1990, when he and his wife were among five Soviet citizens arrested for shoplifting clothes worth 2,000 DM. Belanov protested that he was innocent, and was found guilty, being fined 24,000 DM.<ref name=rp>{{cite news |title=1989: Igor Belanow - Absturz nach Diebstahl |trans-title=1989: Igor Belanov - Collapse after theft|url=https://rp-online.de/nrw/staedte/moenchengladbach/1989-igor-belanow-absturz-nach-diebstahl_aid-20261805 |access-date=23 December 2022 |work=[[Rheinische Post]] |date=9 August 2014 |language=German}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Farrell |first1=Ian |title=The strange case of Igor Belanov – the least remembered Ballon d'Or winner |url=https://www.wsc.co.uk/stories/the-strange-case-of-igor-belanov-the-least-remembered-ballon-d-or-winner/ |access-date=23 December 2022 |work=When Saturday Comes |date=February 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Wilson |first1=Jonathan |title=Behind the Curtain: Football in Eastern Europe |date=9 April 2012 |publisher=Orion |isbn=978-1-4091-0904-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BwXo4iIB6dIC&dq=belanov+wife+shoplifting&pg=PT18 |access-date=23 December 2022 }}</ref> He had faced financial problems due to his demand to be paid in [[U.S. dollar]]s, which he trusted more than the mark, but which had suddenly declined in value.<ref name=rp/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Raack |first1=Alex |title=Fünfzehn Kilo Fleisch|trans-title=Fifteen kilos of meat |url=https://11freunde.de/artikel/f%C3%BCnfzehn-kilo-fleisch/382758 |access-date=23 December 2022 |work=[[11 Freunde]] |date=27 September 2009 |language=German}}</ref>

Belanov moved to [[2. Bundesliga]]'s [[Eintracht Braunschweig]] in January 1991, for a fee of 450,000 DM. He made his debut for his new club on 23 February, and went on to net 21 times in the competition in three seasons combined, also suffering relegation in [[1992–93 2. Bundesliga|1992–93]] without making a single appearance.<ref name=welt>{{cite news |last1=Wallrodt |first1=Lars |title=Der Bundesligastar, der beim Klauen erwischt wurde|trans-title=The Bundesliga star who was caught stealing|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/borussia-moenchengladbach/article116965980/Der-Bundesligastar-der-beim-Klauen-erwischt-wurde.html |access-date=13 October 2024 |work=Die Welt |date=11 June 2013 |language=German}}</ref>

===Retirement===
In 1995 Belanov returned home to Chernomorets for one season, retiring at almost 37 after a spell with [[FC Mariupol|FC Illychivets Mariupol]], appearing in only five games in two seasons combined.

==International career==
In 1983, Belanov was invited to the [[Soviet Union Olympic football team|USSR Olympic team]], for which he played two official matches and two more friendly matches, in which he scored one goal.

In the period 1985–1990 Belanov played 33 matches for the [[Soviet Union national football team|USSR national team]], scoring eight goals. His best performance came at the [[1986 FIFA World Cup]] in Mexico, where he netted four and [[Assist (football)|assisted]] for six others as the team (which comprised 13 Dynamo Kyiv players) reached the [[Single-elimination tournament|round-of-16]]; he scored a [[hat-trick]] in the game against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]], in a losing [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] effort (3–4).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/matches/match=432/index.html |title=Belanov's three not enough to beat brave Belgium |publisher=[[FIFA]]|access-date=11 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120619085534/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/matches/match%3D432/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 June 2012}}</ref>

This performance at the [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]], along with Dynamo's Cup Winners' Cup success, helped Belanov win the [[European Footballer of the Year]] award. He was also part of the squad that reached the final of [[UEFA Euro 1988]], where the national side faced [[Netherlands national football team|the Netherlands]]. With the score at 2–0 for the Netherlands, USSR were awarded a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]]: he took it, but saw [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Hans van Breukelen]] save his effort as the score remained 2–0 until full time, giving the Netherlands the European title.<ref>{{cite web|website=Goal.com|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/476/euro-2008/2008/06/04/723291/tournament-history-euro-1988-west-germany|title=Tournament History: Euro 1988 (West Germany)|date=4 June 2008|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|website=Goal.com |url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/477/euro-2012/2012/06/07/3154962/blast-from-the-past-euro-1988-final-ussr-0-2-netherlands |title=USSR 0–2 Netherlands |access-date=27 June 2013 |archive-date=20 December 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220154626/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/477/euro-2012/2012/06/07/3154962/blast-from-the-past-euro-1988-final-ussr-0-2-netherlands}}</ref> He won 33 caps between 1985 and 1990.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/ibelanov-intlg.html | title = Igor Ivanovich Belanov – International Appearances | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 24 June 2020 | access-date = 29 June 2020 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF.com]]}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Belanov was noted for his athleticism, in particular for his running speed and powerful goal strikes. He was one of the fastest sprinters among Soviet footballers of all times, together with [[Oleg Blokhin|Oleh Blokhin]]. However, while Blokhin was trained by his parents, who were both competitive sprinters, Belanov never received a formal sprint training; yet he ran the 50 metres in a hand-timed 5.7 seconds, corresponding to a mere 0.3 seconds slower than the world record at the time.<ref>[https://www.sports.ru/tribuna/blogs/kleshchonok/2770954.html Блохин и Беланов – главные спринтеры в истории футбола. Пиковый Блохин считался опаснее Кройффа и стоил как Марадона]. sports.ru. 27 April 2008</ref>

==Post-retirement==
===Majority shareholder at Switzerland's FC Wil===
Belanov turned to business after finishing his playing career. He returned to prominence when he became the majority shareholder at Switzerland's [[FC Wil]], in August 2003. His predecessor, banker Andreas Hafen, had been given a five-year prison sentence after embezzling 51 million [[Swiss franc]]s ($40 million) from the ''UBS Bank''.

Belanov's first move at Wil was replacing first-team manager [[Martin Andermatt]] with his former Dynamo Kyiv teammate [[Oleksandr Zavarov]], not taking note of the fact that he lacked the necessary [[UEFA]] licence to manage a European top-division outfit. That circumstance forced Belanov to sign former [[Chemnitzer FC|FC Karl-Marx-Stadt]] manager Joachim Müller. Due to the appointment of Müller, Zavarov's job was officially described as [[director of football]]; Müller did not last long as coach however, as Belanov sacked him just after three months, replacing him with [[:cs:Tomáš Matějček|Tomáš Matějček]].

Matejcek's strict training regiment caused a quick revolt amongst Wil players. This forced Belanov to make amends for his decisions and to re-appoint Müller as manager, and hand the assistant-manager role to former [[Switzerland national football team|Swiss international]] goalkeeper [[Stephan Lehmann]]. Those turned out to be Belanov's last series of actions as Wil's major shareholder as, in a quick sequence, he pulled out of his chairman and shareholder role of the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.11freunde.de/international/124254 |title=Wie sich Igor Belanow seinen Ruf versaute |trans-title=How Igor Belanov ruined his reputation |publisher=[[11 Freunde]] |language=de |date=27 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120601015510/http://www.11freunde.de/international/124254 |archive-date=1 June 2012 |url-status=dead |access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref> Under his leadership, Wil won the [[2003–04 Swiss Cup|Swiss Cup]] for the first time ever, and therefore participated in the [[2004–05 UEFA Cup#Second qualifying round|UEFA Cup qualification]] in the following season.

===Other activities===
Additionally, Belanov also owned a football school in [[Odesa]], Ukraine, which carried his name.

On 1 September 2012, the first twelve commemorative stars were laid on the Alley of Glory of the FC Chornomorets Odesa, one of which is dedicated to Belanov.

In 2018 he joined the board of strategic development [[Ukrainian Association of Football]].<ref>[https://sport.ua/news/421023-belanov-poluchit-dolzhnost-v-ffu Беланов получит должность в ФФУ]. sport.ua. 29 December 2018</ref>

Following the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine 2022]], Belanov joined the [[Territorial Defense Forces (Ukraine)|Territorial Defence Battalion]] of the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian Armed Forces]] of his hometown Odesa.<ref>[https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/ukraine-krieg-igor-belanow-kaempft-gegen-russische-armee-17942111.html ''Früherer Bundesligaspieler kämpft gegen Russen''] [Former Bundesliga player fights Russians] (in German), [[faz.net]], dated 7 April 2022; retrieved 7 April 2022</ref>
